records.name: Marija
records.facts_used: Latin Maria < Greek Mariam/Maria < Hebrew Miryam, meaning uncertain, possibly Egyptian; Bishop Albert at Lateran IV 1215 "land of the Mother"; Terra Mariana; Maarjamaa poetic name since early 20th c.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Kristīne
records.facts_used: Christiana < Christianus; possibly legendary St Christina; Queen Christina of Sweden: throne 1632 at 5, ruled from 18, abdicated 1654, converted, Rome, d. 1689, buried St Peter’s.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Viktorija
records.facts_used: Latin victoria; goddess; 4th-c. N. African martyr; rare in English before Queen Victoria; baptised Alexandrina Victoria 1819 (godfather Alexander I, mother Victoria of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld); reigned 1837-1901; places named after her.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Natālija
records.facts_used: natalis "birthday", Christmas sense; more common in East; St Natalia wife of Adrian of Nicomedia, prison visit disguised, recovered hand; feast 26 Aug Orthodox.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Laura
records.facts_used: laurus laurel, victors’ garlands; 9th-c. Spanish St Laura; English since 13th c.; Petrarch first saw Laura 6 Apr 1327 Sainte-Claire Avignon; Canzoniere 366 poems/317 sonnets; identity uncertain.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Ieva
records.facts_used: Ḥawwa, ḥawa/ḥaya; rare in Middle Ages; ieva = Prunus padus in LV/LT; Siliņš: possible double link, attested Limbaži 1743, calendar 1817.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Anastasija
records.facts_used: Anastasios < anastasis "resurrection" (ana+stasis); St Anastasia of Sirmium d. c.304, relics to Constantinople 5th c., Pharmakolytria, 22/25 Dec.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Diāna
records.facts_used: Roman goddess; dia/diva, dyew-; used since Renaissance; Scott’s Rob Roy (Edinburgh 30 Dec 1817) Diana Vernon; Meredith Diana of the Crossways 1885.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Jūlija
records.facts_used: feminine of Julius; Roman women known by feminine nomen, Major/Minor; Romans 16:15; common in English only since 18th c.; Julia the Elder b. 39 BC, three marriages, exiled 2 BC to Pandateria, Rhegium, d. AD 14.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Linda
records.facts_used: medieval short form of Germanic lind names; coincides with Spanish linda; Kalevipoeg: Linda from grouse egg, wife of Kalev, Toompea mound, Ülemiste from tears (literary events).
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Sandra

records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Marta
records.facts_used: Aramaic mārtā "lady"; Siliņš attested 1591, calendar 1864; Luke 10 and John 11; patron of cooks/housewives; Tarasque legend.
records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Alise

records.name: Sofija

records.name: Ilona

records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Agnese

records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Margarita

records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Rita

records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Lidija

records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Barbara

records.name: Gertrūde

records.reason: Verified in opened sources.

records.name: Jānis
records.facts_used: Yohanan 'Yahweh is gracious' via Ioannes/Iohannes; John the Baptist and apostle John; Siliņš: Jānis also discussed with Janus, no single settled etymology, first written 1290; midsummer 24 June = Jāņi/Joninės/jaanipäev ('John's day'); cheese and beer at Jāņi.
records.next_steps: Hans/Hanss (LV 26 Jan) left out: needs its own short-form story. Wikipedia's claim that Jānis is a 'pre-Christian name' was not used (contested).

records.name: Aleksandrs
records.facts_used: alexo + aner 'defender of men'; Paris; Alexander the Great and medieval tales; Sander Estonian short form; Hittite treaty c.1280 BC with Alaksandu of Wilusa, probably Alexandros, link to Paris uncertain.
records.next_steps: Aleks, Alekss, Aleksis (LV 17 Jul, shared with Aleksejs), Aleksandris, Sandis not included: check Siliņš pages for each before attaching.

records.name: Andrejs
records.facts_used: andreios 'manly'; apostle Andrew first disciple, brother of Peter, Black Sea, X-shaped cross legend, patron of Scotland/Russia/Greece/Romania; Andrejs attested 1204, Andris 1522 (Siliņš); Endrū 'may be' rendering of English Andrew; 30 Nov in all three calendars.
records.next_steps: Andriejus (LT), Andrievs, Andrijs, Andrējs, Andro, Anti not added: verify individually (behindthename lists Anti as Estonian).

records.name: Edgars
records.facts_used: ead + gar; faded after Norman Conquest, revived 18th-19th c. incl. Scott's Bride of Lammermoor (1819); LV calendar 1851, Riga record 1872; Edgar the Peaceful 959-975; Chester 973, six kings per ASC; rowing on the Dee only in 12th-c. writers.
records.next_steps: King Lear connection not used (behindthename only tags it).

records.name: Juris
records.facts_used: georgos 'farmer'; St George Cappadocian soldier, Diocletian, dragon legend, crusaders; Juris/Jurģis attested 1599; Jurģi 23 Apr start of herding season, contract end after serfdom, moving; Jüriöö uprising 1343-1345.
records.next_steps: Jurijs and Georgijs belong to the slavic batch. Jürgen, Jürgo, Jürjo, Jürnas, Jureks, Juriks not verified. A source on the German Jürgen route into Latvian Juris would strengthen paragraph 1.

records.name: Artūrs
records.facts_used: Origin uncertain (artos 'bear' / Artorius); Siliņš: origin not established; Arthurian legend, medieval England, 19th-c. revival; Historia Brittonum 9th c., twelve battles, Badon, 960 men; Geoffrey of Monmouth c.1138; most historians doubt historicity.

records.name: Mārtiņš
records.facts_used: Martinus from Mars; St Martin of Tours cloak legend; Mart Estonian short form (behindthename/name/mart); attested 1601, calendar 1767; Mārtiņi/mardipäev 10 Nov, end of field work, mummers; St Martin feast 11 Nov (LT keeps for Martynas), Protestant shift to 10 Nov = Luther's birthday.
records.next_steps: Martens, Martys, Martinijonas not checked. Mārts/Marts (3 Mar) are a different name day; do not merge without a source.

records.name: Viktors
records.facts_used: Roman cognomen Victor 'conqueror'; early Christians, saints, three popes; rare in medieval England, 19th-c. revival, Victor Hugo; Pope Victor I from Roman Africa, end of 2nd c., dates uncertain; Quartodeciman controversy, rebuked by Irenaeus per Eusebius.
records.next_steps: Viktorijs, Viktorinas not included (need own sources). Pope Victor I and Latin liturgy claim NOT supported by the page; dropped.

records.name: Roberts
records.facts_used: Hrodebert hruod + beraht; Normans to Britain; common 13th-20th c.; LV attested 1545, calendar 1889; Robert the Bruce 1306-1329, Bannockburn 1314, 1328 treaty, heart pilgrimage wish, buried Melrose.
records.next_steps: Roberto (LV) not added; could share entry if a source confirms it as an Italian/Spanish form used in Latvia.

records.name: Kristaps
records.facts_used: Christophoros 'bearing Christ'; figurative early use, literal legend, patron of travellers; Kristaps form of Kristofors attested 1638; Riga giant Kristaps legend (child, gold, city built); early 16th-c. 2.4 m wooden statue in Museum of the History of Riga and Navigation. Film award Lielais Kristaps (est. 1977) dropped to keep sources at 4; could be added with en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lielais_Kristaps.
records.next_steps: Statue date varies in tourist sources (1510/1590/1683); only the museum's 'early 16th century' was used. Kristofs, Kristafors, Krists, Kristo not checked.

records.name: Kārlis
records.facts_used: Karl/Carolus 'man' (alt. 'army'); Charlemagne 742-814; Kārlis attested 1638; coronation 25 Dec 800 by Leo III; Slavic 'king' words from Karolus; died Aachen 28 Jan 814 = Karl name day in LV/EE/Scandinavia (coincidence stated, no causation claimed).
records.next_steps: Karel is also listed in the estonian batch brief; coordinate. Kaarli/Karli left to estonian batch. Latvian 'karalis' and Lithuanian 'karalius' derivation not sourced; not used.

records.name: Nikolajs
records.facts_used: nike + laos; St Nicholas of Myra 4th c., patron of children/sailors/merchants; Klāvs usually linked with Nikolaus but Siliņš also mentions Latvian klāvs 'barn'; dowry legend (disputed); Sinterklaas to Santa Claus; 6 Dec in all three calendars. Klaus = German short form (behindthename/name/klaus); Nigul = Estonian form (behindthename/name/nigul).
records.next_steps: Laas and Niilo (EE 6 Dec) not verified; Niks, Niko, Nikijs, Niklass/Niklāss/Nikolass not checked.

records.name: Miķelis
records.facts_used: Mikha'el 'who is like God?'; only named archangel, Daniel and Revelation; Miķelis attested 1601, Mikus listed under Miķelis; Miķeļi 29 Sep: harvest end, catching Jumis, last courting chance, start of veļu laiks until Mārtiņi, Miķelis in folk songs. Mihkel Estonian form (behindthename/name/mihkel).
records.next_steps: Mihails is in the slavic batch. Mikk, Miko, Miku, Miks, Mikuss, Miķēlis, Mikaels, Mikijs not verified.

records.name: Daniels
records.facts_used: Daniyyel 'God is my judge'; Book of Daniel, Babylonian court, dreams, visions; LV record 1316; Belshazzar's feast, Mene mene tekel upharsin, idiom 'writing on the wall', conflicts with history.
records.next_steps: Taniel dropped: behindthename says it is a Western Armenian transcription, not Estonian. Tanel (EE 11 Dec) may be an Estonian form: needs a source. Daniils/Danils (Russian forms) not included.

records.name: Pēteris
records.facts_used: Petros 'stone' = Aramaic Cephas given to Simon of Bethsaida; Matthew 16:18 wordplay; most prominent apostle; LV name group records from 1292; feast 29 June with Paul; Riga St Peter's: first mentioned 1209, cornerstone of new tower 29 June 1667, destroyed 29 June 1941, rooster 1970 is seventh.
records.next_steps: Peet, Petrs, Petro not verified. Upside-down crucifixion not used (apocryphal).

records.name: Eduards
records.facts_used: ead + weard; Anglo-Saxon kings; one of few Old English names used across Europe; LV calendar 1817, record 1850 Jaunkalsnava; Edward the Confessor 1042-1066, Westminster consecrated 28 Dec 1065, died 5 Jan 1066, Hastings, canonised 1161, Henry III named heir after him, seven later kings.
records.next_steps: Eduars, Edvarts not checked.

records.name: Oskars
records.facts_used: Debated origin (oss + carae / Osgar / Ásgeirr; Siliņš: Old English 'god' + 'spear'); Irish legend son of Oisín; LV calendar 1892; Macpherson's Ossian 1760s, authenticity doubted; Napoleon chose name for Bernadotte's son born Paris 1799, King Oscar I from 1844.
records.next_steps: Godfather claim is presented two ways on Wikipedia (Napoleon vs Joseph Bonaparte); text only says the name was chosen by Napoleon.

records.name: Emīls
records.facts_used: Aemilius, aemulus 'rival'; many European languages; Siliņš allows link with Emīlija, other explanations; LV calendar 1883; Rousseau's Emile (1762), banned and burned in Paris and Geneva, put on the Index; framed as a literary event.
records.next_steps: No source found that Rousseau's book popularised the name; that claim was NOT made. Emīlis, Emīlijs, Emilians/Emiljans not checked.

records.name: Toms
records.facts_used: Aramaic Te'oma 'twin', Didymus; apostle Thomas; Becket boosted English use; Toms recorded 1537; John 20 doubt episode; St Thomas Christian tradition Muziris c.52, killed near Chennai c.72 (disputed); older calendars 21 Dec (kept in LV/EE), modern 3 July (LT Tomas has both).
records.next_steps: Phrase 'doubting Thomas' removed (not in opened source). Tomašs/Tomāšs, Tomijs, Tommi, Toom not checked. Toomas as Estonian form relies on general knowledge; a behindthename/toomas citation would confirm.

records.name: Ēriks
records.facts_used: Eiríkr ei + ríkr; Siliņš: no secure meaning; Scandinavian kings; Erik the Red named Greenland to attract settlers (saga); 18 May = St Eric of Sweden; killed May 1160 near Uppsala after Ascension Mass, legend details partly supported by 2016 bone study; patron of Sweden/Stockholm, coat of arms, relics Uppsala.
records.next_steps: Eerik (EE) not verified.

records.name: Matīss
records.facts_used: Hebrew 'gift of Yahweh'; Matthaios (Matthew) and variant Matthias; Siliņš lists Matīss under Mateuss, possible first record 1388; Motiejus and Mati forms of Matthias; Matthias chosen by lot over Joseph Barsabbas; feast 24 Feb (EE Mati/Matti/Mats) moved to 14 May in 1969 (LT Motiejus has both); LV Matīss 21 Sep = Matthew's feast.
records.next_steps: Matiss (no macron) is not in any calendar, so not keyed. Matis, Mattias, Matas, Mateuss, Matejs, Matvejs not added: check Siliņš and VLKK pages.

records.name: Lembit
records.facts_used: Elder of northern Sakala; chronicle mentions him 14 times in five spellings; killed 21 Sept 1217 at St Matthew's Day battle near Viljandi; linked with lemb 'love' (original form unknown); revived in 19th c.; Jaan Jung's 1880s publication of the chronicle spread his fame.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Kaupo
records.facts_used: Livonian elder of Turaida; uncertain etymology (Jacob short form, merchant/innkeeper, kubjas); Caupo/Kope spellings; Rome 1202-1203 with Bishop Theoderich, Innocent III gave 100 gold coins; mortally wounded 1217, bones buried near Krimulda church; historians divided.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Vambola
records.facts_used: Title hero of Andres Saal's 1889 story (subtitle 1209-1212), trilogy with Aita 1891 and Leili 1892-93; possible models Varbola stronghold or Wamba in Kreutzwald's Lembitu; elder son of the Soontagana elder; earliest bearers in Tartu church registers 1905; destroyer renamed Vambola 1919, sold to Peru 1933.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Vaike
records.facts_used: Coined by Andres Saal for a female character in Vambola (1889); linked with vaikus; counted among proposed reconstructed names (Väike/Vaike); early 20th c. in double names like Vaike-Rosalinde, from 1920 mostly alone.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Aita
records.facts_used: Name came into use after the heroine of Saal's Aita (1891, Tallinn, G. Pihlakas); among proposed reconstructed women's names; Saal's character names given to children for generations.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Leili
records.facts_used: Probably from Laila, also linked with leil; first in Mats Tõnisson's calendar 1884 (24 Sept); spread after Saal's Leili, üks pagana naine (1892-1893); much more common in the first decade of the 20th c.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Meelis
records.facts_used: Linked with meel 'mind'; presumed meaning uncertain; among 19th-century revived names; Enn Kippel's 1941 youth novel Meelis (son of Lembitu, dies defending Tartu 1224 with Vyachko); many reprints; sculpture group on Kassitoome, Tartu.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Salme
records.facts_used: Heroine of the epic folk song (Tähemõrsja) used by Kreutzwald in Kalevipoeg; hen becomes Salme, rejects Moon and Sun, accepts Star (son of the North Star); sometimes linked with salm 'verse'; in Latvia recorded 1914 as of Estonian folkloric origin.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Hämarik
records.facts_used: 'Dusk'; from Faehlmann's literary legend Koit ja Hämarik (first printed 1840, a kunstmuistend that inspired artists); plot; planet XO-4b named Hämarik in IAU NameExoWorlds, chosen by Estonia.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Koit
records.facts_used: 'Dawn'; same Faehlmann legend told from Koit's side (relights the sun); star XO-4 officially named Koit.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Sulev
records.facts_used: Among 19th-century revived old names; Sulevipoeg ('son of Sulev') in Kalevipoeg: courts a hell maiden, rescues another from Tuuslar with Alevipoeg, singes hair on Sädemesaar and lights his pipe, dies in final battle; minehunter EML Sulev.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Leelo
records.facts_used: leelo = folk song in regivärss, leelotamine; Seto refrain / Seto leelo; UNESCO intangible heritage 2009; 'Mother of Song' title at Seto Kingdom Day.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Tarmo
records.facts_used: 'vigour, energy' in Estonian and Finnish; Tarvo dialectal variant; Finnish ships named Tarmo; icebreaker Tarmo (Newcastle 1907), March 1918 seized near Aegna with Svinhufvud aboard disguised as engineer; museum ship in Kotka since 1992.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Joonas
records.facts_used: Finnish/Estonian form of Jonas = Jonah, Hebrew Yona 'dove'; Greek Ionas; cognates; Jonah story (Nineveh, fish, three days); popular in the Middle Ages.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Heiki
records.facts_used: Heinrich < Heimirich (heim + rih); Heiki Estonian form of Heinrich, Enn short form of Hendrik; Henry of Livonia (Henricus de Lettis / Läti Henrik): born c. 1187, ordained 1208, interpreter of legate William of Modena, chronicle c. 1229, priest of Papendorf (Rubene) 1259.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Indrek
records.facts_used: Estonian form of Heinrich, related Hindrek, Ints; Indrek Paas protagonist of vols II-V of Tammsaare's Tõde ja õigus (1926-1933), son of Andres Paas and Mari; 1975 film Indrek based on part II.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Tiidrik
records.facts_used: Dietrich adapted as Tiidrik/Tiidrek; Gothic Þiudareiks 'ruler of the people'; Theodoric the Great; Theoderich of Treiden: priest in Turaida from 1191, first abbot of Daugavgrīva 1202, founded Sword Brothers 1202, bishop of Estonia 1211, killed at Lyndanisse 15 June 1219 on Valdemar II's side.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Ilmar
records.facts_used: Estonian form of Ilmarinen (related Ilmari, Ilmārs); ilma 'air'; Proto-Finnic god-name 'sky-being'; smith who forged sky dome and Sampo; Agricola 1551; Ukko took over weather roles; Muhu song of a 'world-wise smith'.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Ilmatar
records.facts_used: ilma + -tar 'Airess'; virgin air spirit, mother of Väinämöinen in the Kalevala; Lönnrot's depiction as birth-giver of the world based on one runic song; otherwise not connected to creation; Kalevala inspired Kalevipoeg.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Ahto
records.facts_used: Linked with Finnish Ahto, variant of Ahti (sea god), etymology unknown; Idman (Áktios), Ganander 1789, Germanic water words; earliest mention 1551 as giver of fish; Kalevala uses Ahto to avoid confusion with Ahti Saarelainen; wife Vellamo; Kreutzwald used Ahti once in canto 16 of Kalevipoeg; 'Ahti graves'.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Luule
records.facts_used: 'poetry'; first proposed in Mats Tõnisson's calendar, again in 1910 by Oskar Kallas (per Edgar Rajandi, Raamat nimedest, 2011, p. 113, cited on et.wikipedia); Oskar Kallas 1868-1946, first Estonian doctor of folklore 1901, studied Lutsi/Kraasna, envoy, co-founder of ERM, married Aino Kallas.
records.reason: Verified family history written in five languages.

records.name: Heik
records.reason: Shares the 19 January date with Heiki and Enn, but no opened source states that Heik is a form of Heinrich/Hendrik; kept out of the Heiki|Enn entry.
records.next_steps: Check EKI name resources or Edgar Rajandi's Raamat nimedest; if confirmed as a Heinrich short form, add it to the Heiki|Enn key.

records.name: Alev
records.reason: Alevipoeg is a Kalevipoeg character, but no source links the given name Alev to him, and Turkish alev ('flame') is a separate homonym.
records.next_steps: Look for an Estonian onomastic source (Rajandi, EKI) on Alev; write only if the Kalevipoeg link is explicit.

records.name: Olev
records.reason: Olevipoeg (town builder in Kalevipoeg) is documented, but the given name Olev is also linked with Olaf; no opened source states its origin. Status was 'summary'.
records.next_steps: Find a source on Olev < Olaf vs. Olevipoeg and the Tallinn St Olaf (Oleviste) legend.
